result.what_is_wrong: Multiple fairness metrics indicate a measurable adverse impact against the unprivileged group (value "1"): Disparate Impact = 0.8387 (below the 0.95 moderate threshold), Demographic Parity Difference = -0.1526 (the unprivileged group has a ~15.3 percentage-point lower selection rate: 0.7934 vs 0.9459), Equal Opportunity Difference = -0.0866 and Average Odds Difference = -0.1227 (both show lower true-positive performance for group 1), and Theil Index = 0.2808 signals unequal outcome distribution. In addition, there is a severe size imbalance (n=963 for group 1 vs n=37 for group 0) which increases uncertainty in estimates for the small privileged group and complicates reliable comparison.
result.why_is_wrong: Observed disparities are plausibly driven by label/base-rate differences and sample imbalance rather than only random model error. The ground-truth base rates differ markedly (base_rate 0.6926 for group 1 vs 0.8919 for group 0, a 19.9 percentage-point gap), so the model can legitimately learn and reproduce historical outcome patterns (label bias). The 26x group-size imbalance increases variance for metrics of the small privileged group and can make ratios (DI) and differences unstable. Together, these mechanisms (historical label disparities, potential measurement/selection bias, and extreme sample imbalance) explain why the model shows lower selection and lower TPR for the unprivileged group rather than pointing to a single modeling bug.
result.how_to_fix: Start with a pre-processing mitigation that targets label/base-rate dependence: apply AIF360 Reweighing to adjust instance weights so sensitive attribute and label are decorrelated during training. Implement reweighing, retrain, and evaluate on held-out data reporting Disparate Impact, Demographic Parity Difference, Equal Opportunity Difference, Average Odds Difference, and Theil Index with stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. Because the privileged group is very small (n=37), use stratified cross-validation, bootstrap CIs, and consider targeted data collection or careful up/down-sampling (with domain validation) rather than naive oversampling. If residual TPR/FPR gaps remain, use in-processing constrained learning (Fairlearn ExponentiatedGradient with an equalized-odds or TPR constraint) or post-processing (AIF360 EqOddsPostprocessing or CalibratedEqOddsPostprocessing) to enforce specific error-rate parity. Throughout, document accuracy/fairness trade-offs and consult domain experts to verify whether correcting base-rate differences is appropriate for downstream decision-making.
